12-2.solution: He needs 12 working days, worked 3 on and 2 off: days 1 to 3, 6 to 8, 11 to 13 and 16 to 18. The 12th working day is day \(18\).

12-10.solution: Each week has 6 working days, so 42 working days are 7 weeks. The 42nd working day is the 6th day of week 7, calendar day \(6 \times 7 + 6 = 48\); no rest day is needed after it.

12-11.solution: Each 5-hour block is 4 hours of work and 1 of maintenance, so 25 hours hold 5 blocks and 20 working hours: \(20 \times 80 = 1600\) units.

12-18.solution: The first 3 days give \(20 \times 3 \times 8 = 480\) man-hours, leaving \(720\). 15 workers at 6 hours do \(90\) a day: \(8\) days.

12-23.solution: The efficiencies are \(100\%, 95\%, \ldots, 55\%\), which add to \(\frac{10(100 + 55)}{2} = 775\%\). The output is \(50 \times 7.75 = 387.5\) units.

12-24.solution: The project is \(8 \times 20 = 160\) hours of work. 12 days at 8 hours give 96, leaving 64; at 10 hours a day that is \(6.4\) days, ending on day \(18.4\), \(1.6\) days before the deadline.

12-26.solution: Phase 1 (2 parts) is \(8 \times 15 = 120\) worker-days, so one part is 60. Phase 2 is \(180\), \(15\) days for 12 workers; phase 3 is \(300\), \(15\) days for 20. Total \(15 + 15 + 15 = 45\) days.
